body:
#21788 suppresses the `UV_NATIVE_TLS` deprecation warning whenever `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` is present, but effective-value resolution only consumes `Some(true)` for `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` before falling through to `UV_NATIVE_TLS`.

That leaves this case:

```sh
UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=false UV_NATIVE_TLS=true uv ...
```

The warning is suppressed because `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` is present, but deprecated `UV_NATIVE_TLS=true` still makes the effective `system_certs` value true.

This also differs from the intended behavior described on #21788: if `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` is set, `UV_NATIVE_TLS` should be ignored entirely.

Expected: explicit `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=false` wins and the deprecated variable is ignored. If the deprecated variable is still allowed to control the result, the warning should not be suppressed.
title: UV_SYSTEM_CERTS=false can still fall through to UV_NATIVE_TLS=true without warning
